subject: english
title: Snake Bite
author: Shankar (from 'Life with Grandfather')
instructions: Literature practice for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Identify the following sentences as True or False.

questions.q: Raja caught a small snake in a coconut shell.
Grandfather kept the snake as a pet.
A bee stung Raja on his finger.
Grandmother knew that it was only a bee sting.
Grandfather did not allow Raja to speak at the old man's house.
The old man used modern medicines to treat Raja.
Grandfather sent gifts to the old man.

sections.title: Match the character (or speaker) with the description.

questions.answer: Raja — the narrator, an adventurous boy

questions.right: believed to cure snake bite with mantras
questions.answer: The old grey-haired man — believed to cure snake bite with mantras

questions.right: carried Raja to the medicine man
questions.answer: Grandfather — carried Raja to the medicine man

questions.right: cried for help when Raja showed her the snake he had caught
questions.answer: Grandmother — cried for help when Raja showed her the snake he had caught

sections.title: Read the passage and fill in the blanks.

questions.q: Raja tried to catch a ________ in the evening.
It stung him on his ________.
Grandmother thought that he had been bitten by a ________.

sections.passage: Later in the evening, I tried to catch a bee and it stung me on my finger. I felt a sharp pain. I ran to grandmother and told her that I had been bitten and wanted her to do something to stop the pain. Grandmother thought that I had been bitten by a snake. She called out to Grandfather, "Come and see what has happened to Raja."

sections.title: Read the passage and fill in the blanks.

questions.q: The old man took water in a small ________ vessel.
He started reciting some ________.
Raja could not talk because Grandfather held him ________.

sections.passage: The old man then took some water in a small brass vessel, sat in front of us and started reciting some mantras. I wanted to tell him that it was a bee and not a snake that had bitten me. But Grandfather held me tight and did not allow me to talk.

questions.q: Raja's grandparents are concerned about his ________.
Raja's ________ throws the shell away.
Raja's grandfather advises him never to go near a ________ again.
The snake hid itself in a ________.
Grandfather ran across the garden and through the ________ fields.

sections.title: Answer in one or two sentences (about 30 words).

questions.q: What bit Raja and what did Grandmother think?
questions.answer: A bee stung Raja on his finger. Grandmother thought that he had been bitten by a snake.

questions.q: Why did Grandfather throw away the coconut shell?
questions.answer: Raja had trapped a snake in it. Grandfather believed all snakes were very dangerous, so he snatched the shell and threw it away to protect Raja.

questions.q: Why could Raja not tell the old man that a bee had stung him?
questions.answer: Grandfather held him tight and did not allow him to talk; the old man had also told him to sit still and keep quiet.

questions.q: What did the old man say after the 'treatment'?
questions.answer: He said, 'Thank God, you brought Raja in time. He is out of danger now. It was indeed a poisonous snake that bit him.'

questions.q: Why did Grandfather send gifts to the old man?
questions.answer: Grandfather believed that the old man had saved Raja from a poisonous snake bite by his 'magic cure', so he sent him gifts out of gratitude.

questions.q: What lesson do we learn from the story 'Snake Bite'?
questions.answer: We learn that timely communication is important and silence is not always good, and that we should not put blind faith in untrained medicine men but seek proper treatment.

questions.q: How did the old man treat the boy for snake bite?
questions.answer: He made Raja sit still on Grandfather's lap, took water in a small brass vessel and recited mantras. After a few minutes he washed Raja's finger, gave him water to drink and asked him to keep quiet. Then he declared that Raja was out of danger.

or.q: What was the 'magic cure' that the grey-haired old man performed on Raja? Was it really a cure?
or.answer: He recited mantras over water in a brass vessel, then washed Raja's finger and gave him water to drink. It was not a real cure — Raja had only been stung by a bee and the pain had already stopped; the 'cure' was superstition.

questions.q: Do you approve of Grandfather not letting Raja speak? Give reasons.
questions.answer: No. If Raja had been allowed to speak, he could have explained that a bee, not a snake, had stung him. The family would have been spared fear and worry, and the old man's false 'cure' would have been exposed. Children should be listened to, especially in an emergency.
